claim: Zebrafish Zbtb14 protein shares 70% homology to its human counterpart ZBTB14
source: Zebrafish Zbtb14 protein shares 70% homology to its human counterpart ZBTB14.
evidence: Direct statement in the text comparing sequence homology between species

claim: Zebrafish and human ZBTB14 proteins bear a nearly identical N-terminal BTB motif and five consecutive C-terminal zinc finger motifs
source: The two transcription factors bear a nearly identical N-terminal BTB motif and five consecutive C-terminal zinc finger motifs (Figure 1A).
evidence: Stated in text and supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 1A

claim: A significant increase of macrophage markers including mfap4, csf1ra, and mpeg1.1 was observed from 19.5 hpf to 3 dpf in zbtb14-deficient embryos and larvae
source: A significant increase of macrophage markers including mfap4, csf1ra, and mpeg1.1 (Meijer et al., 2008; Spilsbury et al., 1995; Zakrzewska et al., 2010) was observed from 19.5 hr post-fertilization (hpf) to 3 days post-fertilization (dpf) (Figure 2A–G' and H).
evidence: Experimental observation supported by WISH data and citations to prior work characterizing these markers

claim: mfap4 is a macrophage marker
source: A significant increase of macrophage markers including mfap4, csf1ra, and mpeg1.1 (Meijer et al., 2008; Spilsbury et al., 1995; Zakrzewska et al., 2010) was observed from 19.5 hr post-fertilization (hpf) to 3 days post-fertilization (dpf) (Figure 2A–G' and H).
evidence: Characterized as a macrophage marker with supporting citations

claim: csf1ra is a macrophage marker
source: A significant increase of macrophage markers including mfap4, csf1ra, and mpeg1.1 (Meijer et al., 2008; Spilsbury et al., 1995; Zakrzewska et al., 2010) was observed from 19.5 hr post-fertilization (hpf) to 3 days post-fertilization (dpf) (Figure 2A–G' and H).
evidence: Characterized as a macrophage marker with supporting citations

claim: mpeg1.1 is a macrophage marker
source: A significant increase of macrophage markers including mfap4, csf1ra, and mpeg1.1 (Meijer et al., 2008; Spilsbury et al., 1995; Zakrzewska et al., 2010) was observed from 19.5 hr post-fertilization (hpf) to 3 days post-fertilization (dpf) (Figure 2A–G' and H).
evidence: Characterized as a macrophage marker with supporting citations

claim: The expanded macrophage population was confirmed in zbtb14-/-//Tg(mpeg1.1:eGFP) larvae
source: This expanded macrophage population was further confirmed in zbtb14-/-//Tg(mpeg1.1:eGFP) larvae (Figure 2I–J' and K).
evidence: Experimental confirmation using transgenic reporter line

claim: zbtb14-deficient macrophages can migrate toward wounds as wild type macrophages do
source: It is worth noting that the zbtb14-deficient macrophages could still migrate toward the wound as wild type ones did, implying their function remains intact (Figure 2L–M').
evidence: Experimental observation from wound migration assay

claim: zbtb14-deficient macrophages retain intact function
source: It is worth noting that the zbtb14-deficient macrophages could still migrate toward the wound as wild type ones did, implying their function remains intact (Figure 2L–M').
evidence: Inference based on normal wound migration behavior

claim: apoeb is a specific microglia marker
source: In addition, WISH with apoeb probe (a specific microglia marker) and neutral red vital dye staining revealed an expansion of microglia (the macrophages that reside in brain) in zbtb14-deficient larvae (Figure 2N–Q' and R).
evidence: Stated as a specific marker for microglia

claim: Microglia are macrophages that reside in brain
source: In addition, WISH with apoeb probe (a specific microglia marker) and neutral red vital dye staining revealed an expansion of microglia (the macrophages that reside in brain) in zbtb14-deficient larvae (Figure 2N–Q' and R).

claim: An expansion of microglia was observed in zbtb14-deficient larvae
source: In addition, WISH with apoeb probe (a specific microglia marker) and neutral red vital dye staining revealed an expansion of microglia (the macrophages that reside in brain) in zbtb14-deficient larvae (Figure 2N–Q' and R).
evidence: Experimental observation using WISH and neutral red staining

claim: Many more macrophages were found in zbtb14-/-//Tg(mpeg1.1:eGFP) zebrafish than in controls in adult WKM samples (1.82% mpeg1.1+ versus 0.50% mpeg1.1+)
source: The myeloid cell fraction was analyzed, and many more macrophages were found in zbtb14-/-//Tg(mpeg1.1:eGFP) zebrafish than in controls (1.82% mpeg1.1+ versus 0.50% mpeg1.1+) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1S–T' and U)
evidence: Quantitative FACS analysis data from adult zebrafish

claim: The development of macrophages originated from HSCs are affected in zbtb14 mutants
source: The myeloid cell fraction was analyzed, and many more macrophages were found in zbtb14-/-//Tg(mpeg1.1:eGFP) zebrafish than in controls (1.82% mpeg1.1+ versus 0.50% mpeg1.1+) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1S–T' and U), indicating that the development of macrophages originated from HSCs are also affected.
evidence: Inference from adult macrophage expansion data

claim: Only the development of monocyte/macrophage lineage is affected in the absence of zbtb14
source: In addition, the expressions of neutrophil and erythrocyte markers during primitive hematopoiesis stage, as well as those of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, neutrophil, erythrocyte, and lymphocyte markers during definitive hematopoiesis stage were all normal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1). These observations suggest that only the development of monocyte/macrophage lineage is affected in the absence of zbtb14.
evidence: Experimental data showing normal expression of other lineage markers

claim: A significant increase of pH3+GFP+ double-positive cells were observed in zbtb14-/-//Tg(mpeg1.1:eGFP) larvae compared to controls
source: A significant increase of pH3+GFP+ double-positive cells were observed in zbtb14-/-//Tg(mpeg1.1:eGFP) larvae compared to those in controls (Figure 3A–C' and D).

claim: TUNEL assay results could not show discernible differences in the percentage of TUNEL+GFP+ cells in zbtb14-/-//Tg(mpeg1.1:eGFP) larvae compared to controls
source: Nevertheless, the results from TUNEL assay could not show discernible differences in the percentage of TUNEL+GFP+ cells in zbtb14-/-//Tg(mpeg1.1:eGFP) larvae compared to the percentage in controls (Figure 3E–G' and H).

claim: The expanded macrophage population is due to enhanced proliferation
source: These data suggest that the expanded macrophage population is due to enhanced proliferation.
evidence: Inference from pH3 and TUNEL assay results

claim: The proportion of immature progenitors was obviously increased in zbtb14 mutants compared with the siblings
source: The results revealed that the proportion of immature progenitors (with a round-shape morphology and a higher nuclear/cytoplasm ratio) was obviously increased in zbtb14 mutants compared with the siblings (Figure 3J).
evidence: Experimental data from MGG staining and morphological analysis

claim: The proportion of fully differentiated macrophages was decreased in zbtb14 mutants
source: By contrast, the proportion of fully differentiated macrophages was decreased in the mutants (Figure 3J).
evidence: Experimental data from MGG staining and morphological analysis

claim: The expansion of macrophage lineage is mainly due to excessive monocyte/macrophage progenitor proliferation in zbtb14 mutants
source: Based on these observations, we can draw the conclusion that the expansion of macrophage lineage is mainly due to excessive monocyte/macrophage progenitor proliferation in zbtb14 mutants.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from pH3, TUNEL, and MGG staining data

claim: The monocyte/macrophage abnormalities in zbtb14-deficient larvae could be effectively rescued with zebrafish zbtb14 mRNA
source: The monocyte/macrophage abnormalities in zbtb14-deficient larvae could be effectively rescued with either zebrafish zbtb14 or human ZBTB14 mRNA, confirming the specificity and conservation of ZBTB14 proteins (Figure 4A–D and F).

claim: The monocyte/macrophage abnormalities in zbtb14-deficient larvae could be effectively rescued with human ZBTB14 mRNA
source: The monocyte/macrophage abnormalities in zbtb14-deficient larvae could be effectively rescued with either zebrafish zbtb14 or human ZBTB14 mRNA, confirming the specificity and conservation of ZBTB14 proteins (Figure 4A–D and F).

claim: ZBTB14 proteins are functionally conserved between zebrafish and humans
source: The monocyte/macrophage abnormalities in zbtb14-deficient larvae could be effectively rescued with either zebrafish zbtb14 or human ZBTB14 mRNA, confirming the specificity and conservation of ZBTB14 proteins (Figure 4A–D and F).

claim: ZBTB14 displays an activation or inhibition effect on different promoters
source: ZBTB family proteins are frequently described as transcription repressors, nevertheless, ZBTB14 displays an activation or inhibition effect on different promoters (Kaplan and Calame, 1997).

claim: DAXX is a transcription corepressor
source: To distinguish the activity of Zbtb14 on transcription, the repression domain of DAXX (a transcription corepressor) (Zhou et al., 2006) was fused in frame with Zbtb14 (DAXX-Zbtb14), which forced the fusion protein to be a potent repressor.

claim: DAXX-zbtb14 mRNA had an obvious rescue effect as wild type zbtb14 mRNA
source: In vivo rescue assays demonstrated that DAXX-zbtb14 mRNA had an obvious rescue effect as wild type zbtb14 mRNA (Figure 4E and F)

claim: Zbtb14 acts as a negative regulator in monocyte/macrophage development
source: In vivo rescue assays demonstrated that DAXX-zbtb14 mRNA had an obvious rescue effect as wild type zbtb14 mRNA (Figure 4E and F), implying Zbtb14 acted as a negative regulator in monocyte/macrophage development.

claim: Multiple important regulators involving monocyte/macrophage development including pu.1, csf1ra, csf1b, il34, mafb, klf4, irf8, and c-myc were upregulated in zbtb14-deficient macrophages
source: The differentially expressed genes (DEGs) analysis of the RNA-seq data indicated that multiple important regulators involving monocyte/macrophage development including pu.1, csf1ra, csf1b, il34, mafb, klf4, irf8, and c-myc were upregulated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).

claim: pu.1 is a pivotal transcription factor which can promote macrophage proliferation
source: The expression level of pu.1, the pivotal transcription factor which can promote macrophage proliferation (Dai et al., 2002), was obviously increased.

claim: The expression level of pu.1 was obviously increased in zbtb14-deficient macrophages
source: The expression level of pu.1, the pivotal transcription factor which can promote macrophage proliferation (Dai et al., 2002), was obviously increased. Such upregulation was further confirmed by real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) analyses (Figure 4G).

claim: The signals of pu.1 were clearly intensified from 18 to 22 hpf in zbtb14-deficient embryos compared with wild type ones
source: In addition, WISH analyses showed that the signals of pu.1 were clearly intensified from 18 to 22 hpf in zbtb14-deficient embryos compared with the wild type ones (Figure 4H–K' and L).

claim: pu.1 is a major direct target of Zbtb14
source: Since Zbtb14 was identified as a transcription repressor, we postulated that pu.1 would be a major direct target of Zbtb14, whose derepression in the absence of Zbtb14 probably contributed to the expansion of monocyte/macrophage population.
evidence: Hypothesis based on repressor function and expression data

claim: Zbtb14 displayed a significant repression effect on the zebrafish pu.1 promoter in luciferase assays
source: To test this hypothesis, a –0.6 kb zebrafish pu.1 promoter in luciferase reporter was co-transfected with zbtb14 expressing plasmid in HEK293T cells. As anticipated, luciferase analyses showed that Zbtb14 displayed a significant repression effect (Figure 4M).

claim: The pu.1 promoter region could be specifically co-immunoprecipitated with GFP-Zbtb14 in vivo
source: Next, in vivo chromatin immunoprecipitation polymerase chain reaction (ChIP-PCR) was conducted in zebrafish larvae expressing GFP or GFP-Zbtb14 using an anti-GFP antibody. In this experiment, the pu.1 promoter region could be specifically co-immunoprecipitated with GFP-Zbtb14 (Figure 4N).

claim: A prominent rescue effect could be obtained with a dominant-negative Pu.1 plasmid injection in zbtb14 mutants
source: To further demonstrate that pu.1 was upregulated in macrophage lineage, a series of in vivo experiments was performed. A prominent rescue effect could be obtained with a dominant-negative Pu.1 plasmid (the DBD domain of Pu.1 was under the control of mpeg1.1 gene's promoter, cloned in TOL2 backbone) injection in zbtb14 mutants (Figure 4O and F).
evidence: Experimental rescue data with dominant-negative construct

claim: Macrophages are reduced in zebrafish pu.1Δ371 mutant line
source: Moreover, we took advantage of a zebrafish pu.1Δ371 mutant line (a truncated Pu.1 whose transactivation activity was reduced) in which macrophages were reduced (Yu et al., 2017; Figure 4P and F)
evidence: Cited from prior work and confirmed by experimental data

claim: No obvious alleviation could be found in zbtb14-/-//pu.1Δ371 double mutant zebrafish
source: Moreover, we took advantage of a zebrafish pu.1Δ371 mutant line (a truncated Pu.1 whose transactivation activity was reduced) in which macrophages were reduced (Yu et al., 2017; Figure 4P and F), and no obvious alleviation could be found in zbtb14-/-//pu.1Δ371 double mutant zebrafish, indicating zbtb14 was epistatic to pu.1 (Figure 4Q and F).
evidence: Experimental data from double mutant analysis

claim: zbtb14 is epistatic to pu.1
source: Moreover, we took advantage of a zebrafish pu.1Δ371 mutant line (a truncated Pu.1 whose transactivation activity was reduced) in which macrophages were reduced (Yu et al., 2017; Figure 4P and F), and no obvious alleviation could be found in zbtb14-/-//pu.1Δ371 double mutant zebrafish, indicating zbtb14 was epistatic to pu.1 (Figure 4Q and F).
evidence: Inference from double mutant genetic analysis

claim: Zbtb14 regulates monocyte and macrophage development through inhibiting the expression of pu.1
source: In summary, these findings suggest that Zbtb14 regulates monocyte and macrophage development through inhibiting the expression of pu.1.
evidence: Summary conclusion from multiple experimental approaches

claim: Protein SUMOylation is catalyzed by a sequential enzymatic cascade including E1 (SAE1/SAE2), E2 (UBC9), and E3
source: Similar to ubiquitination, protein SUMOylation is catalyzed by a sequential enzymatic cascade including E1 (SAE1/SAE2), E2 (UBC9), and E3 in which SUMO (Small Ubiquitin-like MOdifier) molecules are covalently attached to lysine residues within substrate proteins (Eifler and Vertegaal, 2015).

claim: SUMOylation is generally associated with transcriptional repression through the recruitment of corepressors such as NCoR and SMRT
source: The SUMOylation is generally associated with transcriptional repression through the recruitment of corepressors such as NCoR and SMRT (Garcia-Dominguez and Reyes, 2009; Valin and Gill, 2007).

claim: A weak adduct band approximately 10 kD larger than unmodified Zbtb14 protein was observed
source: We have mentioned above the presence of a weak adduct which was ~10 kD (the size of one SUMO molecule) larger than the unmodified Zbtb14 protein (Figure 1D).

claim: The adduct band of Zbtb14 became much more intensive in the presence of UBC9 and SUMO1
source: To validate this hypothesis, zbtb14-expressing plasmid was transfected with or without UBC9 and SUMO1 in HEK293T cells. Western blot analyses showed that the adduct band became much more intensive in the presence of UBC9 and SUMO1 (Figure 5A, lanes 1 and 2).

claim: SUMO1 molecules could be coprecipitated with Zbtb14
source: Furthermore, immuno-coprecipitation assays showed that SUMO1 molecules could be coprecipitated with Zbtb14 (Figure 5B, lane 1).

claim: Zbtb14 can be SUMOylated in cells
source: These results indicated that Zbtb14 could be SUMOylated in cells.
evidence: Conclusion from western blot and co-IP experiments

claim: K40 is the SUMOylated site in Zbtb14
source: We carried out a series of mutations and finally found that the adduct band of Zbtb14K40R mutant was abolished (Figure 5A, lanes 3–6), suggesting K40 was the SUMOylated site.
evidence: Experimental data from mutagenesis and western blot

claim: The Zbtb14K40R mutant protein was located in the nucleus as wild type Zbtb14
source: HA-tagged Zbtb14 and Zbtb14K40R were transfected in HEK293T cells, respectively. The results from immunofluorescence analyses revealed that the mutant protein was located in the nucleus as wild type Zbtb14 (Figure 5C).

claim: Zbtb14 and SUMO1-Zbtb14K40R displayed a strong repression effect on the pu.1 promoter
source: Next, luciferase reporter assays with the –0.6 kb zebrafish pu.1 promoter were carried out. While Zbtb14 and SUMO1-Zbtb14K40R (SUMO1 molecule was fused in frame with Zbtb14K40R to mimic the SUMOylated Zbtb14) displayed a strong repression effect, Zbtb14K40R completely lost the ability to repress transcription (Figure 5D).

claim: Zbtb14K40R completely lost the ability to repress transcription
source: Next, luciferase reporter assays with the –0.6 kb zebrafish pu.1 promoter were carried out. While Zbtb14 and SUMO1-Zbtb14K40R (SUMO1 molecule was fused in frame with Zbtb14K40R to mimic the SUMOylated Zbtb14) displayed a strong repression effect, Zbtb14K40R completely lost the ability to repress transcription (Figure 5D).

claim: Both zbtb14 and SUMO1-zbtb14K40R mRNAs had a remarkable rescue effect in zbtb14-deficient larvae
source: Finally, in vivo rescue assays were conducted in zbtb14-deficient larvae with zbtb14, zbtb14K40R, and SUMO1-zbtb14K40R mRNA, respectively. As expected, both zbtb14 and SUMO1-zbtb14K40R mRNAs had a remarkable rescue effect, whereas zbtb14K40R mRNA did not (Figure 5E and F).

claim: zbtb14K40R mRNA did not have a rescue effect in zbtb14-deficient larvae
source: Finally, in vivo rescue assays were conducted in zbtb14-deficient larvae with zbtb14, zbtb14K40R, and SUMO1-zbtb14K40R mRNA, respectively. As expected, both zbtb14 and SUMO1-zbtb14K40R mRNAs had a remarkable rescue effect, whereas zbtb14K40R mRNA did not (Figure 5E and F).

claim: SUMOylation of Zbtb14 is pivotal for transcription repression
source: Taken together, these results suggest that SUMOylation of Zbtb14 is pivotal for transcription repression.
evidence: Conclusion from luciferase and rescue experiments

claim: A missense mutation, ZBTB14S8F, was detected in a de novo AML patient
source: A missense mutation, ZBTB14S8F, was detected in a de novo AML patient (Tyner et al., 2018).

claim: Wild type ZBTB14 mRNA significantly rescued the expanded macrophage population in zbtb14-deficient zebrafish
source: To assess the role of the mutant protein, we first performed in vivo rescue assays in zbtb14-deficent zebrafish. While the wild type ZBTB14 mRNA significantly rescued the expanded macrophage population, the mutant failed to display any rescue effect (Figure 6A and B)

claim: ZBTB14S8F mutant failed to display any rescue effect in zbtb14-deficient zebrafish
source: To assess the role of the mutant protein, we first performed in vivo rescue assays in zbtb14-deficent zebrafish. While the wild type ZBTB14 mRNA significantly rescued the expanded macrophage population, the mutant failed to display any rescue effect (Figure 6A and B), implying that the normal functions of ZBTB14 was lost.

claim: The normal functions of ZBTB14 are lost in the ZBTB14S8F mutant
source: While the wild type ZBTB14 mRNA significantly rescued the expanded macrophage population, the mutant failed to display any rescue effect (Figure 6A and B), implying that the normal functions of ZBTB14 was lost.

claim: The transcription level of ZBTB14S8F is comparable to that of wild type ZBTB14
source: Next, we investigated the reason underlying the defects of the ZBTBS8F mutant. Although its transcription level was comparable to that of wild type ZBTB14 (Figure 6C)

claim: ZBTB14S8F protein could hardly be detected by western blot analysis
source: Although its transcription level was comparable to that of wild type ZBTB14 (Figure 6C), ZBTB14S8F protein could hardly be detected by western blot analysis, implying that the stability of the mutant protein was impaired (Figure 6D, lane 4).

claim: The stability of the ZBTB14S8F mutant protein is impaired
source: Although its transcription level was comparable to that of wild type ZBTB14 (Figure 6C), ZBTB14S8F protein could hardly be detected by western blot analysis, implying that the stability of the mutant protein was impaired (Figure 6D, lane 4).

claim: Bafilomycin, but not MG132, inhibited ZBTB14S8F protein turnover
source: We thus treated ZBTB14S8F-expressing HEK293T cells with MG132 (a proteasomal inhibitor), or bafilomycin (an autophagy inhibitor). The results indicated that bafilomycin, but not MG132, inhibited ZBTB14S8F protein turnover (Figure 6D, lanes 7 and 10)

claim: The ZBTB14S8F mutant protein might be subjected to autophagic degradation
source: The results indicated that bafilomycin, but not MG132, inhibited ZBTB14S8F protein turnover (Figure 6D, lanes 7 and 10), suggesting that the mutant protein might be subjected to autophagic degradation.

claim: The turnover of both ZBTB14S8A and ZBTB14S8D mutant proteins kept normal
source: Since serine is most frequently modified with phosphorylation, which could affect the protein stability, ZBTB14S8A and ZBTB14S8D mutants were constructed to mimic the dephosphorylated or constitutively phosphorylated status of ZBTB14. However, the turnover of both two mutant proteins still kept normal (Figure 6D, lanes 2 and 3).
evidence: Western blot data from mutant analysis

claim: The LIR/AIM motif contains the consensus sequence [W/F/Y]xx[L/I/V]
source: The LIR/AIM motif contains the consensus sequence [W/F/Y]xx[L/I/V] (Popelka and Klionsky, 2015).

claim: The S to F mutation (FETI) forms a φxxΨ motif
source: We noticed that the S to F mutation (FETI) happened to form a φxxΨ motif, which was probably the reason why the ZBTB14S8F mutant protein was targeted to undergo autophagic degradation.

claim: The turnover of ZBTB14S8W and ZBTB14S8Y mutant proteins was comparable to that of ZBTB14S8F mutant protein
source: To further validate this point, ZBTB14S8W and ZBTB14S8Y mutants were also constructed and expressed in HEK293T cells. The results from western blots showed that the turnover of the two proteins was comparable to that of ZBTB14S8F mutant protein (Figure 6D, lanes 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, and 12).
evidence: Western blot data from mutant analysis

claim: The serine to phenylalanine mutation impairs the protein stability of ZBTB14
source: Overall, the serine to phenylalanine mutation impairs the protein stability of ZBTB14, which probably contributes to AML pathogenesis.

claim: The serine to phenylalanine mutation probably contributes to AML pathogenesis
source: Overall, the serine to phenylalanine mutation impairs the protein stability of ZBTB14, which probably contributes to AML pathogenesis.
evidence: Speculation based on loss of protein stability

claim: Zbtb14 is absolutely required for proper monopoiesis during primitive hematopoiesis
source: Zbtb14 is absolutely required for proper monopoiesis during primitive hematopoiesis, which is reflected by the expansion of macrophage population in zbtb14 mutant embryos/larvae compared to wild type ones from 19.5 hpf to 3 dpf.

claim: The requirement of Zbtb14 continues to definitive hematopoiesis since HSCs-derived macrophages remain hyperproliferative in zbtb14-/- adults
source: Such a requirement of Zbtb14 continues to definitive hematopoiesis since HSCs-derived macrophages remain hyperproliferative in zbtb14-/- adults.

claim: zbtb14 is indispensable for the maintenance of proper quantity of monocytes/macrophages
source: Hence, zbtb14 is indispensable for the maintenance of proper quantity of monocytes/macrophages.
evidence: Conclusion from developmental and adult data

claim: The zbtb14-deficient mpeg1.1+ cells can be recruited to the wound and result in normal healing
source: Functionally, the zbtb14-deficient mpeg1.1+ cells can still be recruited to the wound, and result in a normal healing, implying these macrophages are able to terminally differentiate into mature cells.
evidence: Experimental observation from wound healing assay

claim: zbtb14-deficient macrophages are able to terminally differentiate into mature cells
source: Functionally, the zbtb14-deficient mpeg1.1+ cells can still be recruited to the wound, and result in a normal healing, implying these macrophages are able to terminally differentiate into mature cells.

claim: The abnormal expansion of macrophages is mainly due to excessive monocyte/macrophage progenitor proliferation in zbtb14 mutants
source: The results from anti-pH3 and MGG staining assays indicate that the abnormal expansion of macrophages is mainly due to excessive monocyte/macrophage progenitor proliferation in zbtb14 mutants.
evidence: Conclusion from pH3 and MGG staining data

claim: csf1ra, csf1b, and il34 are M-CSFR signaling genes
source: In addition, DEGs analyses of RNA-seq data further indicate several key regulators involved in macrophage proliferation such as csf1ra, csf1b, and il34 (M-CSFR signaling genes) (Dai et al., 2002), and pu.1 (Celada et al., 1996) are all significantly upregulated.

claim: csf1ra, csf1b, il34, and pu.1 are all significantly upregulated in zbtb14-deficient macrophages
source: In addition, DEGs analyses of RNA-seq data further indicate several key regulators involved in macrophage proliferation such as csf1ra, csf1b, and il34 (M-CSFR signaling genes) (Dai et al., 2002), and pu.1 (Celada et al., 1996) are all significantly upregulated.

claim: pu.1 is a direct target of Zbtb14
source: The mechanistic studies identify that pu.1 is a direct target of Zbtb14.
evidence: Conclusion from luciferase and ChIP experiments

claim: PU.1 is an ETS family transcription factor
source: As a pivotal ETS family transcription factor, PU.1 is implicated in multiple stages of hematopoiesis such as generation of early myeloid progenitors, cell fate determination of granulocytic versus monocytic lineages of neutrophil-macrophage progenitors, maintenance of the accessibility of macrophage-specific genes during monocytic differentiation (Kastner and Chan, 2008).

claim: PU.1 is implicated in multiple stages of hematopoiesis
source: As a pivotal ETS family transcription factor, PU.1 is implicated in multiple stages of hematopoiesis such as generation of early myeloid progenitors, cell fate determination of granulocytic versus monocytic lineages of neutrophil-macrophage progenitors, maintenance of the accessibility of macrophage-specific genes during monocytic differentiation (Kastner and Chan, 2008).

claim: The development of neutrophil lineage kept normal in zbtb14 mutants
source: It is worth noting that while the aberrant macrophage expansion could be effectively rescued with dominant-negative Pu.1 (TOL2-mpeg1.1:pu.1-DBD), the development of neutrophil lineage still kept normal in zbtb14 mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-A'', B).

claim: The overexpression of full-length pu.1 in wild type embryos could induce an expansion of macrophage population without interfering neutrophil lineage development
source: In parallel, the overexpression of full-length pu.1 (TOL2-mpeg1.1:pu.1) in wild type embryos could induce an expansion of macrophage population without interfering neutrophil lineage development (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C-D', E).

claim: zbtb14 transcripts were constantly higher in mpeg1.1+ cells than in mpx+ cells at different developmental stages
source: In addition, we compared the expression level of zbtb14 in mpeg1.1+ and mpx+ cells at different developmental stages, and found zbtb14 transcripts were constantly higher in the former (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: RT-qPCR data from sorted cell populations

claim: Zbtb14 is a macrophage lineage-specific transcription factor
source: These observations suggest that Zbtb14 is a macrophage lineage-specific transcription factor.
evidence: Inference from lineage-specific expression and functional data

claim: PU.1 is a predicted upstream transcription factor of mammalian ZBTB14
source: Meanwhile, we also investigated the transcriptional network that involved zbtb14. Bioinformatic analyses show that PU.1 is a predicted upstream transcription factor of mammalian ZBTB14.

claim: PU.1 displayed a significant repression effect on the zebrafish zbtb14 promoter
source: The promoter region of zebrafish zbtb14 was cloned into a reporter vector, and luciferase assay showed that PU.1 displayed a significant repression effect on it (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).

claim: A Zbtb14-Pu.1 negative feedback loop might regulate monocyte and macrophage development
source: Therefore, a Zbtb14-Pu.1 negative feedback loop might regulate monocyte and macrophage development.
evidence: Speculation based on mutual repression data

claim: Approximately 20 genes including CEBPA, RUNX1, FLT3, DNMT3A, and NPM1 are most frequently mutated in AML patients
source: Approximately 20 genes including CEBPA, RUNX1, FLT3, DNMT3A, and NPM1 are most frequently mutated in AML patients (Ley et al., 2013).

claim: Some rare mutations can be found in few AML samples
source: Nevertheless, some rare mutations can be found in few samples (Ley et al., 2013).

claim: Wild type ZBTB14 mRNA displayed a similar rescue effect as zbtb14 in zebrafish
source: In the current study, we took advantage of the zbtb14-deficient zebrafish line to demonstrate the functional conservation between the human ZBTB14 and the zebrafish ortholog zbtb14. While wild type ZBTB14 mRNA displayed a similar rescue effect as zbtb14, the ZBTB14 mutant was shown to be a loss-of-function transcription regulator in monocyte/macrophage development.

claim: The ZBTB14S8F mutant is a loss-of-function transcription regulator in monocyte/macrophage development
source: While wild type ZBTB14 mRNA displayed a similar rescue effect as zbtb14, the ZBTB14 mutant was shown to be a loss-of-function transcription regulator in monocyte/macrophage development.

claim: The protein stability of ZBTB14S8F is profoundly affected due to aberrant autophagy
source: Furthermore, we demonstrated that the protein stability of ZBTB14S8F was profoundly affected due to aberrant autophage.

claim: ZBTB14 was originally cloned as a transcriptional repressor gene on the murine c-MYC promoter
source: ZBTB14, originally named as ZF5, was cloned as a transcriptional repressor gene on the murine c-MYC promoter (Yanagidani et al., 2000).

claim: C-MYC amplification was identified in some AML patients
source: C-MYC amplification was identified in some AML patients (Tang et al., 2021).

claim: c-MYC is one of the most overexpressed genes in AML
source: Moreover, c-MYC is one of the most overexpressed genes in AML (Handschuh et al., 2018).

claim: Either increased expression or aberrant activation of c-MYC plays important roles in leukemogenesis
source: Either increased expression or aberrant activation of c-MYC plays important roles in leukemogenesis (Salvatori et al., 2011).

claim: c-myc was upregulated in zbtb14-deficient macrophages
source: RNA-seq and RT-qPCR experiments showed that c-myc was upregulated in our zbtb14-deficient macrophages (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).

claim: Znf161 knockout mice had a defect in genomic instability, which was associated with higher cancer risk
source: In addition, it has been reported that Znf161 (another alias of Zbtb14) knockout mice had a defect in genomic instability, which was associated with higher cancer risk (Kim et al., 2019).

claim: ZBTB14 would be a tumor suppressor
source: These results suggest that ZBTB14 would be a tumor suppressor, whose inactivity is tightly related with AML pathogenesis in humans.
evidence: Speculation based on multiple lines of evidence

claim: ZBTB14 inactivity is tightly related with AML pathogenesis in humans

source: Here, we report that the deficiency of zbtb14, a transcription repressor gene belonging to ZBTB family, leads to an aberrant expansion of monocyte/macrophage population in zebrafish.

claim: Hematopoiesis is the process by which hematopoietic stem cells proliferate and differentiate into all blood lineages
source: Hematopoiesis is the process by which hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) proliferate and differentiate into all blood lineages.

claim: Hematopoiesis is driven by a variety of transcription factors, which function in a stage and lineage-specific manner
source: It is driven by a variety of transcription factors, which function in a stage and lineage-specific manner (Bodine, 2017).

source: Most tissue-resident macrophages arise from the blood islands of the yolk sac (Kurotaki et al., 2017).

source: Yet, monocytes in circulation are derived from HSCs, which give rise to monocytes in a step-wise manner via common myeloid progenitors, granulocyte-monocyte progenitors, monocyte-dendritic cell progenitors, and common monocyte progenitors (Hettinger et al., 2013).

claim: ZBTB16 plays roles in both normal and malignant hematopoiesis in humans
source: Several members of ZBTB family transcription factors including ZBTB16 (also known as promyelocytic leukemia zinc finger) (Sobas et al., 2020), ZBTB27 (also known as B cell leukemia/lymphoma 6) (Nakamura, 2000), ZBTB7 (also known as leukemia/lymphoma-related factor) (Constantinou et al., 2019), and ZBTB15 (also known as T-helper-inducing POZ/Kruppel-like factor) (Taniuchi, 2016) play various roles in both normal and malignant hematopoiesis in humans.

claim: At least 12 Zbtb genes are involved in hematopoietic development in mice
source: In addition, at least 12 Zbtb genes are involved in hematopoietic development in mice (Maeda, 2016).

claim: ZBTB14 is expressed in a variety of blood cell types
source: ZBTB14, a ZBTB family member whose function has been poorly characterized, is expressed in a variety of blood cell types (The Human Protein Atlas).

claim: Mutation of ZBTB14 has not previously been identified in AML
source: Recently, a missense mutation of ZBTB14 gene (ZBTB14S8F) was detected by whole-exome sequencing in a newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patient (Tyner et al., 2018). Note that mutation of ZBTB14 has not previously been identified in AML.

claim: The potential role of ZBTB14 in hematopoiesis and leukemogenesis was obscure
source: Nevertheless, the potential role of ZBTB14 in hematopoiesis and leukemogenesis was obscure, (Yin et al., 2015).

claim: The zebrafish serves as an ideal model organism for hematopoietic development and disease studies
source: The zebrafish serves as an ideal model organism for hematopoietic development and disease studies (Gore et al., 2018).

claim: Ten nucleotides were deleted in the zbtb14 mutant, which resulted in a truncated protein with only 80 amino acids by frameshifting
source: Ten nucleotides were deleted, which resulted in a truncated protein with only 80 amino acids by frameshifting (Figure 1B and C).

claim: Zebrafish hematopoiesis consists of primitive and definitive waves which occur sequentially in distinct anatomical sites
source: Like mammalian hematopoiesis, zebrafish hematopoiesis consists of primitive and definitive waves which occur sequentially in distinct anatomical sites (Galloway and Zon, 2003; Zon, 1995).

claim: The primitive hematopoiesis gives rise to embryonic myeloid cells (neutrophils and macrophages) and erythrocytes from the rostral blood island and intermediate cell mass
source: The primitive hematopoiesis gives rise to embryonic myeloid cells (neutrophils and macrophages) and erythrocytes from two intraembryonic locations, the rostral blood island (the equivalent of mammalian yolk sac) and intermediate cell mass.
evidence: General biological knowledge about zebrafish development

claim: The definitive HSCs initiate within the ventral wall of the dorsal aorta
source: The definitive HSCs which give rise to all blood lineages initiate within the ventral wall of the dorsal aorta (a tissue analogous to the mammalian aorta/gonad/mesonephros), then translocate to the caudal hematopoietic tissue (the equivalent of fetal liver) and colonize in kidney marrow (the equivalent of bone marrow) in adults (Bertrand et al., 2008; Bertrand et al., 2007).

claim: The primitive macrophages cannot sustain for a long period, which will eventually be replaced with HSC-derived macrophages as definitive hematopoiesis begins
source: The primitive macrophages cannot sustain for a long period, which will eventually be replaced with HSC-derived macrophages as definitive hematopoiesis begins (Xu et al., 2012).

claim: zbtb14 mutant zebrafish were viable and fertile
source: Since zbtb14 mutant zebrafish were viable and fertile, the whole kidney marrow (WKM) samples were collected from wild type Tg(mpeg1.1:eGFP) and zbtb14-/-//Tg(mpeg1.1:eGFP) lines in adults.
